title: MV Damocles Legacy | 3D First-Person Blobber | In Development

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
A
retro
3D First-Person Dungeon Crawler
with Turn-Based Combat, inspired by Etrian Odyssey, Classic 90's crawlers like Wizardry and Might & Magic, Trials of Mana, and Octopath Traveller.
The main gameplay loop is a narrative where you, an experienced field marshal, are given the duty to create a party and delve a giant mysterious dungeon. For that, there are
10 unique characters
available that all have extensive personalities and backstory, and from them you
recruit 4
to take with your custom player character. We're going for
high character customisation
here, with lots of viable builds for people to try, but also interesting characters and a grand story, mixing what I consider to be the best of blobbers and JRPGs. This is in a high-magic, high-fantasy setting with some dramatic political intrigue, as well as potential romance elements.
VIDEO NOTES:
Please keep in mind,
this video is showcasing early dev-stage work
. Lots of assets will be tweaked, and I'm aware the start is a bit wordy. Jump to
39:47
to go straight to dungeons/combat, if that's the part that interests you most.
There will actually be an action prologue between the character creation and the bit in the Consolate, but it's not ready at the moment. I've also noticed some pretty gnarly bugs just in the recording of this video, because of course they stayed hidden to the last moment (haha), but many of these are actually now fixed. Combat also defo needs some serious tweaking (and lots of skills are a bit dodgy too, man am I annoyed Sacrifice is broken again lol). And darn Bitdefender decides "I'm going to update right now!" in the middle of the recording as well (the odds are insane).
Yep, I figured its time to throw a thread down here. I didn't want to until I had a video and was sure this was something I was commited to. Honestly, I didn't think I'd make a whole game. Early last year, I would have laughed at the prospect, when I was thinking of making a new project (I'm an author of a
fairly popular Classic Doom Mod, Walpurgis
, which hit 1.0 in May last year). But, there were things I could never manage to quite do in a mod, and as I reviewed things I could do, various stars aligned to conspire me to walk this road. So in September 2025, I just went 'F it, we ball' and started. Considering the work involved, it's actually come a huge way since then. ETA? No idea yet, though early 2027 is a wild spitball estimate.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
Today's work.
So I was thinking this morning. Sure, I know what each character does, and sure, asking them for information about themselves during recruitment gives hints in a narrative way which I personally kind of like an enjoy.
But if the player isn't me, and wants a precise mechanical rundown of what this character does? What if they want to meticulously plan their party choices? There are players who like more crunchy but transparent systems (and this game does have detailed party builds as one of the core concepts).
Well, the first solution I came up with is this, which shows a quick summary of the character during the recruit scene, and you can click the option to temporarily add the character to inspect them.
Some people have already informed me, mind, that this seems too dense as it is (and it needs to black out the background to reduce loudness, which I agree with).
I am looking into to other options.
So what are people's thoughts here?
Way too dense? Should I just let the player add the character to party to inspect them only? Should I instead use an item that calls up this information rather than hanging it onto recruitment conversations?

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
Today's Work
Not alot, due to being tired from work. Basically just bugfixing Klaryn's Chronomancy, which was all successful, actually, pretty happy about that.
Chronomancy's core is a unique ability to 'Congeal Time', which blurs Her Highnesses battle sprite, and gives her a barrier against incoming damage. She can then choose to use this barrier as a resource to heal or use other support effects (but in so doing, reduce her own protection, and though she wears Mail, she's otherwise got quite low defences).
One of the big things I'm going for in this game is that all the healing abilities have caveats, and all the damage abilities usually do better when you meet certain requirements.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
Commander Skill Tree
for the player's avatar is basically done.
Some of the other abilities:
If you've seen the main video, you'll know the player has a bunch of background choices, but no matter your choices, you're a
Sky Marshal
of Tessalatoria, a trusted military commander.
Isn't it funny how 15 year old kids always get their village torched, and go on to become heroes in JRPGs? Well, I'm totally switching that around here. Your main character is 27, and they're here due to driving their way ambitiously to the top already. They have still done so in impressive time, but in a place of continual conflicts, with the ability to often get merits, it's entirely concievable, right?
In any case, the Commander tree is for players who want a support focused main. There are powerful party-wide buffs and solid healing abilities. But equally, you can also focus on DPS (with Bladework), and Tanking (with Bulwark). And indeed, you can hybrid your build as well.
Though not all recruitable characters are as versatile in role as the MC, they do still have a similar ability to focus or diversify in their builds to filll gaps in your team. Most skills in this have 3-5 ranks too, with usually quite a boost by the top rank, if you invest deep into a favourite ability.

Passive Skills are a go!
There are 20 Generic Passives shared between the 10 characters, and then each character has 4 unique passives (which are what goes into those bottom slots, not ready yet). Where those passives appear also varies and that determines the required investment in the tree as a whole (e.g. Klaryn above gets Charismatic, Litheness, and Iron Will on Tier I, so they're available immediately. Jeorges also has Litheness, but it's tier III, so he'd first have to spend 4 points on his lower tiers to get Litheness).
Some of the normal skill-trees do have the occasional passive too, but those are unique to those trees and directly interact with that trees mechanics normally.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
A quick tour of the jungle stratum:
An early version of this was shown in the first preview video, but it's been developed a fair bit since then. Caverns now darken when you enter, water is in 3D, there's more ambience, and the level is much less of a sprawl, and more interconnected. More is still to be done here (probably light shafts and a mild heat-haze if I can, possibly water shaders), but I think it looks like a cool compromise of modern and retro now, doesn't it?
One of the big gameplay elements we will see in this game is choosing a route.
The main dungeon is sub-divided into stratums of three floors a piece (a bit like Etrian Odyssey, if you have played it). But, it's also different. All parties will have the same experience in floors 1-3, but for floor 4, you will pick between delving into The Dark Morass (Jungle) or The Howling Dunes (Desert) for your next stratum.
You'll be locked with your choice for another 3 floors, culminating in a unique boss for that stratum. Items you can gather (and hence equipment you'll use) will also be different, and there will be different themed puzzles too. Then, the two branches re-join, have 3 floors which are same for all, and then again, a split will occur where you choose. This will happen a total of three times in game.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
New video with more character recruitment scenes (for Klaryn, Alistair, Avon, and Mihoshi).
As previously mentioned, picking your party is a big element of this game. There are 10 characters, each with unique stories, interactions, and skill trees. This kind of element take hints from Trials of Mana/Seiken Densetsu III, and Octopath Traveller, though with more story and some Persona like elements in character development. Also replayability, of course, for those interested in such things.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
Klaryn's Unique Passive Skills:
Klaryn's Chronomancy and Congealed Time has already been discussed somewhat, but as a reminder: it acts a resource that also shields her from damage, basically as additional HP.
Imperator Charges are a new mechanic I've added in for her Royal Skill-Tree. Some skills build charges on success (usually attacks or orders). Each charge gives her some Physical Power, Agility, and HP Regen, but other skills can spend them for powerful effects (i.e. giving a large Critical boost to an attack, giving the charges buff temporarily to all allies, healing all allies based on charges spent etc.).

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
More shots of the Desert, The Howling Dunes (there was one on my profile post):
You may notice the heat-haze is now in, warping this screenie a bit, looks pretty good in motion.
A suspicious swirly pool of sand I can jump in, you say? Surely nothing can go wrong?
Well, no indeed, it takes us to the ruins segment, a whole extra map beneath the sands:
Since the desert is subdivided by lots of sheer cliffs, you'll have to use the under-ruins to bridge the surface (early on you gain an artifact to swim up falling columns of sand).
The goal is to find the three Sphinxes and solve their riddles (or just beat the snot out of them, though they're tough!), which is turn tells you how to get out of this floor.

posts.author: Social_Knight
posts.body:
Welp, my good 'ol PC finally bit the bucket on Friday. Having to make a new build in the midst of stupid RAM prices is just my luck, but here we are, new builds done and we're back.
Naturally, this means a slight delay of a few days where I've done basically squat (nothing was lost, though, the game was stored on my secondary SSD and backed up on my external).
As a bonus, the performance on my game is now flawless lol. I guess I'm still not mad at making optimisations like I did; it means those with mediocre rigs can still get 40 FPS on the most taxing sections of geometry.
The less good is that my old Photoshop CS6 licence from antiquity in my student days is dead and refuses to work, so I guess I'm migrating to Krita, which will lead a bit of slower artwork production as I adapt to new software.
